brief: A base with a bay bin in one half of its cell.

requirements.requirement: Bay bin filling one half of a cell position
requirements.evidence: bay:0#0,0#bay4 (hex-bin-bay-s-half-solid, a half bay tray) sits at cell (0,0,0) and fills the south half of that position.

The configurator won't put a bay inside a base's own cell. Bay sockets only show up at an empty cell position with bases on three of its sides. A single full base got no offers, and neither did a half-n base sharing the bay's cell. So the bay hangs off three full bases: piece:1,0,0, piece:0,1,0 and piece:-1,1,0.
check_build: ok, meshClash clear, no errors. The only info note is that 11 open faces could take caps.

finish.summary: I built a half bay tray (hex-bin-bay-s-half-solid) that fills one half of the empty position at cell (0,0). It isn't on a single base, though: the configurator won't put a bay inside a base's own cell. A bay only fits in an empty position with bases on three sides, so I placed three full bases around it, at (1,0), (0,1) and (-1,1). Placing two of them gave LOOSE_BODY warnings. The bay bolts to all three bases. check_build passes with meshClash clear and no errors. The only note is that 11 open faces could take caps. If you meant an ordinary half-width bin inside one base, that's also possible (for example hex-bin-half-e-full).

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
